blocks.prompt: 3 (a) In how many different ways can the following persons sit in a round table? Hint (Solve according to both the cases): 8 persons
blocks.explanation:
8 persons around a round table: a circular permutation.
The hint asks for both cases.
Plan: fix one person, arrange the others; then halve for Case-II.
steps:
Given: \(n = 8\) persons at a round table.
To find: the number of seatings in Case-I and in Case-II.
Method: Case-I (clockwise and anticlockwise orders different): \((n - 1)!\). Case-II (clockwise and anticlockwise orders identical): \(\dfrac{(n - 1)!}{2}\).

Case-I
\[(8 - 1)! = 7! = 5040\]
Why: Rotating everyone one seat gives the same seating, so we fix one person and arrange the other 7 in the remaining seats.

Case-II
\[\dfrac{(8 - 1)!}{2} = \dfrac{5040}{2} = 2520\]
Why: Each clockwise order and its anticlockwise mirror are now the same, so every seating was counted twice.

Check
\[8! \div 8 = 5040 \;\checkmark\]
Why: 8! seatings in a row; each circular seating appears as 8 rotations.
